worldSettings.title: World Settings
worldSettings.subtitle: Your in-game world settings. Hover over field names for a detailed description.
worldSettings.emptyCategory: There are no settings in this category
palette.descriptionBold: Block mappings allow you to turn one block into another.
palette.descriptionRest: Blocks which match the input will be turned into the output, states which are not set will also be converted where possible.
palette.unavailable: Block Mapping is currently not available for the current world input/output format.
biome.descriptionBold: Biome mappings allow you to turn one biome into another.
biome.descriptionRest: Biomes which match the input will be replaced with the output during conversion.
biome.unavailable: Biome Mapping is currently not available for the current world input/output format.
dimensions.title: Dimensions/Pruning
dimensions.subtitle: You can change one dimension to another, you can also enter co-ordinates of chunks you want to include in the conversion.
dimensions.noteRest: Chunker does not provide datapacks to load custom dimensions, please ensure they are present before loading the world.
custom.identifier.description: Namespaced identifier in the format namespace:id (can't be a vanilla dimension).
custom.fallbackBiome.description: The biome used as a fallback for padding / when a biome can't be converted.
pruning.description: Whether chunk pruning should include or exclude regions, off indicates no pruning.
region.name.description: The internal name used for this region, useful for if you're exporting your Chunker settings.
region.minChunkX.description: The X co-ordinate of the chunk, you can get this by dividing X by 16
region.minChunkZ.description: The Z co-ordinate of the chunk, you can get this by dividing Z by 16
region.maxChunkX.description: The X co-ordinate of the chunk, you can get this by dividing X by 16
region.maxChunkZ.description: The Z co-ordinate of the chunk, you can get this by dividing Z by 16
converter.subtitle: This tab allows you to disable/enable some of the features on the world converter, doing so may lead to faster conversions but lower quality.
converter.customIdentifiers.description: Whether custom identifiers outside the minecraft namespace are allowed to be read / written. This should be disabled if you want to prevent modded blocks from being converted.
converter.blockConnections.description: When reading legacy/bedrock worlds, block-connections are used to connect chests/fences/panes, this can hold neighbouring chunks from being converted but greatly increases conversion accuracy as blocks on the edge can have data fetched from surrounding chunks.
converter.itemConversion.description: Whether converting items should be enabled.
converter.lootTableConversion.descriptio: Whether the converter should attempt to match structure loot table files.
converter.mapConversion.description: Whether converting in-game maps should be enabled.
converter.discardEmptyChunks.description: Whether empty chunk data should not be written.
converter.preventYBiomeBlending.descript: Whether empty chunks should be padded at the top of each column to prevent vertical biome blending (Java only).
converter.enableCompact.description: Compacts the database at the end, may cause longer conversion times.
converter.exportPreloadTooltip: Placing these files in the same directory as your level.dat will load them when the world is loaded with Chunker.
converter.exportCliTooltip: Allows you to get your current settings as CLI usage.
converter.readmeTxt: Please copy the .json files in this folder to the same directory as your level.dat, Chunker will automatically preload these when you select your world.
cli.title: Export Settings for CLI
cli.subtitle: This screen allows you to view your current settings as a CLI command.
cli.commandTooltip: You can use this command with the CLI to replicate your current settings. You will need to make sure the paths are correct.
cli.outputFormat.tooltip: This is the output format for the world.
cli.converterSettings.tooltip: This is the settings from the Converter Settings tab.
cli.worldSettings.tooltip: This is the NBT settings which are written from the World Settings tab.
cli.dimensionMappings.tooltip: These are the mappings on how it should map dimensions from the Dimensions tab.
cli.pruning.tooltip: These are the mappings on how it should prune dimensions from the Dimensions tab.
cli.dimensionRegistry.tooltip: These are definitions for the custom dimensions to be used in the input/output.
cli.biomeMappings.tooltip: These are the biome mappings which define how they should be changed from input to output.
cli.blockMappings.tooltip: These are the block mappings generated from the Block Mapping tab.
